# Women's Fashion & Beauty — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Beauty & Personal Care: typically around 1,000, most listings 300–13,000 (117 listings)
- Traditional Wear: typically around 3,000, most listings 550–4,250 (91 listings)
- Western Wear: typically around 1,000, most listings 400–2,750 (39 listings)
- Bags & Accessories: typically around 475, most listings 140–2,200 (26 listings)
- Baby Girl's Fashion: typically around 1,000, most listings 270–2,000 (19 listings)
- Jewellery & Watches: typically around 1,250, most listings 335–4,300 (18 listings)
- Wholesale - Bulk: typically around 2,200, most listings 800–3,800 (11 listings)
- Footwear: typically around 750, most listings 480–3,000 (7 listings — thin data)

Winter Wear has too few listings for reliable ranges — use general judgment there.
This is a low-ticket category, so a cheap price alone is normal, not a scam signal. The exception is items claimed as high-value (genuine gold jewellery, branded watches/bags) priced far below any plausible market value — that is a scam signal, hold. Where n < 10, the ranges are thin; lean on general judgment.

## What good listings look like
- "Gold plated Chura" — NPR 600
- "Maharani saree" — NPR 1,500
- "Teej special offers saree" — NPR 1,050
- "saree for karwachauth" — NPR 2,999
- "kurtha tops" — NPR 1,250

A good listing names the item type plus one anchor: material (gold plated), occasion (Teej, Karwa Chauth), or style/fit. Terse titles ("tops") are common and routinely approved here — photos carry the detail — so a short title alone is never grounds to hold.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Jewellery claimed as genuine gold/silver/gemstone but priced in the plated/imitation range above (most jewellery listed here IS plated) — misrepresentation risk; hold unless the listing clearly says plated or imitation.
- Beauty products making medicinal claims — skin-whitening injections/glutathione drips, weight-loss or "guaranteed result" pills — these are health products, not cosmetics; hold.
- "Original" imported branded cosmetics (MAC, Huda, SK-II, Kylie, etc.) at a small fraction of retail — the classic fake-cosmetics pattern in Nepal; hold.

No editor rejections are recorded for this category to date; approvals skew lenient, so hold sparingly beyond the signals above.
